title: Avalo Therapeutics to Participate in the BTIG Biotechnology Conference
summary: WAYNE, Pa., July 22, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Avalo Therapeutics, Inc. (Nasdaq: AVTX), a clinical stage biotechnology company fully dedicated…...
body_text: Avalo Therapeutics to Participate in the BTIG Biotechnology Conference July 22, 2026 7:00am EDT WAYNE, Pa., July 22, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Avalo Therapeutics, Inc. (Nasdaq: AVTX), a clinical stage biotechnology company fully dedicated to developing therapeutics targeting the IL-1β pathway for immune-mediated inflammatory diseases, today announced that Dr. Garry Neil, Chief Executive Officer of Avalo, will participate in the “Honing in on Hidradenitis” panel at the virtual BTIG Biotechnology Conference on Wednesday, July 29, 2026, at 10:30 am ET. Management will also host one-on-one investor meetings during the conference. Live webcasts and replays, when available, can be found under "News / Events" in the Investors section of the Avalo Therapeutics website at https://ir.avalotx.com. The archived webcast will be available for replay for at least 30 days. About Avalo Therapeutics Avalo Therapeutics is a clinical stage biotechnology company fully dedicated to developing therapeutics targeting the IL-1β pathway for immune-mediated inflammatory diseases. Our lead asset, abdakibart, is an anti-IL-1β monoclonal antibody (mAb). Positive topline data was recently reported for abdakibart in a Phase 2 clinical trial in hidradenitis suppurativa (HS). In addition to HS, we’re exploring additional opportunities to make an impact in prevalent indications that have significant remaining unmet needs. We are also advancing AVTX-010, a long-acting next-generation anti-IL-1β mAb designed to extend dosing intervals and build upon the differentiated profile established by abdakibart. For more information about Avalo, please visit www.avalotx.com . For media and investor inquiries Christopher Sullivan, CFO Avalo Therapeutics, Inc. ir@avalotx.com 410-803-6793 or Meru Advisors Lauren Glaser lglaser@meruadvisors.com Source: Avalo Therapeutics Released July 22, 2026

body_text: Listen on Apple Podcasts Listen on Spotify Watch on YouTube Subscribe to START ‍ A phone call used to mean trust. Now it could be AI. title: Start Your LLC in Michigan: A Step-by-Step Guide
summary: Discover everything you need to know about an LLC in Michigan, including key features, how to form one, common pitfalls to avoid, and more.
body_text: Michigan LLC tax and legal considerations There are some key things to keep in mind regarding the tax and legal environment in the Great Lakes State. Federal and state taxes As a pass-through entity, the income and losses of the LLC are reported on the individual members' personal federal and state income tax returns. In Michigan, the flat income tax rate is 4.25%. Michigan also offers a state-specific tax election for pass-through entities, including LLCs, known as the Flow-Through Entity (FTE) tax. This was created in 2021 as a response to the federal 2017 Tax Cuts and Jobs Act’s state and local tax (SALT) deduction cap of $10,000. (Note that the 2025 One Big Beautiful Bill Act increased the limit to $40,000, but it is set to decrease to $10,000 by 2030.) The purpose of the FTE is to allow certain business owners to pay tax at the entity level, essentially reducing their amount of pass-through income and subsequent federal taxes owed. Eligible entities who can apply for this FTE tax credit are: S corporations Partnerships LLCs that file federal income tax returns as partnerships Businesses who choose to elect into the FTE tax must do so through the Michigan Treasure Online portal , typically by March 15 of the tax year, and reelect every three years. Local taxes Along with state income tax, LLC members may also have to pay local income tax depending on where they live. There are 24 cities in Michigan that levy income tax, including East Lansing, Flint, Pontiac, and more. The tax rate varies by municipality; for example, East Lansing income tax is 1% for residents and 0.5% for nonresidents. Local business licenses Some cities and counties require business licenses to be able to operate there. Even if the city in which you conduct business doesn’t require you to obtain business licenses, you may still be required to obtain an industry-specific license or permit. For instance, in Bay City, Michigan, companies don’t need a general business license, but those that operate food trucks or pedicabs must apply for separate licenses. Common mistakes to avoid The following are some common pitfalls that should be avoided when forming your LLC in Michigan: Failing to file the annual statement. To stay compliant and in active status, LLCs in Michigan must regularly file an annual statement. The statement is due by February 15 every year, and the filing fee is $25. Picking the wrong business name. Adhere to Michigan’s specific LLC naming requirements (noted earlier). Mixing personal and business finances. Open a separate bank account to track all business expenses and make payments. Not having an operating agreement. Having a readily accessible, written operating agreement can help you settle disputes that may arise over financial agreements and other potential litigation. Otherwise, the courts make determinations based on Michigan state law, not necessarily what is in the best interest of the LLC. Not fulfilling all licensing requirements. Follow your specific industry and profession’s licensing requirements, and ensure that if you form a PLLC, all members are licensed in the specific service. How much does it cost to form an LLC in Michigan? The cost to form an LLC in Michigan is only $50 to file the articles of organization, making it a very affordable place to start a business. However, many LLC owners choose additional services. Here’s the complete breakdown. Name reservation: $25 filing fee Formation cost: $50 for filing the articles of organization Certificate of good standing: $50 filing fee Business licenses and permits: Varies by profession, business activity, and area Registered agent service: $249 per year on average Operating agreement: $99 and up for an online service Business insurance: Varies depending on the insurance company and type of insurance, but generally between $40 and $70 per month, per policy The total cost to start an LLC in Michigan ranges from $50 to more than $400 if you take advantage of all the professional services available. Once you set up your LLC, you’ll also need to file your annual statement for a filing fee of $25 each year. Is a Michigan LLC right for you? The legal business entity you choose should fit your business and financial needs. It’s important to consider all that goes into forming and maintaining an LLC to determine if it’s right for you. When a Michigan LLC is the best choice When you operate as a sole proprietorship vs. LLC, you take on more personal liability, meaning your personal assets could be used to settle business debts and obligations. While an LLC requires submitting formal LLC formation documents to the Michigan Corporation Division and annual legal requirements, you can still be a single-member LLC and safeguard your personal assets. Operating as an S corp vs. LLC can be beneficial if you need investors to help grow the business or want to issue stock. However, LLCs have fewer requirements and regulations, enjoy more flexible management structures and profit distributions, and have greater flexibility with tax elections. Even if you form an LLC, you can elect to be taxed as an S corporation. When another state might be better If you decide not to form an LLC in Michigan, there are other states that could be good picks for various reasons: Delaware : Business-friendly tax and legal environment, no franchise tax, option for series LLCs, privacy on formation documents Arizona : No annual franchise tax, no annual report requirements, and low-cost formation fees Florida : No personal income tax and low costs of formation

title: Amazon OpenSearch UI now supports one-click dashboard migration
summary: Discover more about what's new at AWS with Amazon OpenSearch UI now supports one-click dashboard migration
body_text: Amazon OpenSearch Service now supports one-click migration from legacy OpenSearch Dashboards to OpenSearch UI, for both OpenSearch domains and serverless collections. OpenSearch UI is the new, zero-downtime, serverless interface for search and unified observability across multiple data sources. With this launch, the multiple tenants and thousands of saved objects you created in legacy OpenSearch Dashboards become reusable in your OpenSearch UI applications, reducing the operational complexity of moving between interfaces. With one-click migration, you can move your existing tenants and saved objects into OpenSearch UI workspaces without recreating them manually. The mechanism works for OpenSearch Dashboards created under Amazon OpenSearch Service domains and serverless collections. You can migrate everything into a new workspace or into an existing one. If you have created multiple tenants in your OpenSearch Dashboard, you have the option to either convert them into a single workspace or keep them separate for different teams. This feature is available in all AWS Regions where OpenSearch UI is available. To get started, see Using OpenSearch UI in the Amazon OpenSearch Service Developer Guide. Visit the OpenSearch UI Help page for detailed feature tutorials. To learn more about the service, see the Amazon OpenSearch Service product page .

title: OTR fuel cards: How to manage trucking expenses, support drivers, and protect your bottom line
summary: Discover how a fuel card can help you save money, get cash to your truck drivers, reduce fraud, and improve your bottom line.
body_text: Share Managing a trucking business means controlling costs and maintaining oversight on fuel spend. It also means helping drivers out on the road as unexpected expenses arise. In this article we’ll cover some ways a fuel card program helps you keep costs down, keeps your drivers operating at maximum capacity, and keeps your business running smoothly. Learn about how to save on fuel with this blended fleets white paper Explore strategies to manage fuel costs for blended fleets, and optimizing savings with the use of a fuel card. Learn more What to look for in an OTR fuel card At a time when fuel prices continue to fluctuate, shopping around is more important than ever. Most fuel cards offer fueling and maintenance at a network of truck stops nationwide. The perks vary widely, so it’s important to shop around for the right card for your business. Things to look for include: Discounts or rewards on fuel and maintenance Fraud protection Roadside assistance Detailed Level III reporting Other ways to economize and become more efficient through fleet card use include managing truck repair and service costs. These charges add up quickly and become a drain on fleets of any size. However, optimizing your fleet with regular preventative maintenance will catch problems early before a driver is broken down on the road or you’re faced with a large, unexpected repair bill. How OTR fuel cards help control costs Fuel discounts and expense tracking Fuel cards are the perfect solution for OTR businesses spending large amounts of money on fuel every year. Not only are these cards convenient for your drivers, they also have easy expense tracking and reporting features . You’ll have access to a network of stations and truck stops where your drivers can refuel and get routine maintenance done all in one place. Fleet cards can be like business credit cards for drivers, offering significant fuel and maintenance discounts and an ability to purchase items beyond just fuel. Fleet managers can place different controls on their drivers’ fleet cards depending on the driver. Cards can be used strictly for fuel and maintenance, or you might have a policy that allows drivers to buy drinks and snacks with their fuel cards. The cards are connected to each driver or truck and there are fraud protection features that check your driver’s identity at the pump . Maintenance records and route optimization Maintaining a full maintenance record covering each truck in your fleet will help you stay on top of vehicle needs. Ensuring there are extra trucks on hand to replace those in the shop can save fleets lost road time. Scheduling planned maintenance also reduces vehicle wear and tear. Another cost-saver is delivery route optimization. Saving both time and money, mapping out the most efficient routes and stops will save your business thousands of dollars over a given fiscal year. By leveraging available technology combined with your fleet card program, you are making a valuable investment in your business and in your drivers, making their job easier. Fleet analytics and reporting WEX analytics and reporting tools provide easy access to insights that can lead to greater profitability. Available insights include fuel card purchase monitoring and driver tracking. Having access to this information helps fleet managers cut costs, streamline fleet operations, and uncover savings. You’ll find new ways to forecast and budget expenses, spot any unusual activity or misuse, compare performance with other fleets, and provide accurate fuel tax reporting . How to get cash to your drivers on the road Fuel card cash advances An easy and secure way for your drivers to get cash while on the road is through a fleet card. If a trucker needs a cash advance, you can pre-load your WEX fleet cards with funds. This allows drivers to get cash at participating truck stops without a fee. Drivers don’t have to purchase anything – they just pick up the cash and head on down the road. There are also checking options that come with some fleet card programs. Additionally, drivers can use the WEX OTR fuel card at participating ATM machines if they need cash while on the road. This card can be used at PLUS Network ATM machines or Interlink debit sites for a fee with every transaction. As an added benefit, these cash transactions are documented and will appear in your reporting. This helps ensure driver accountability, and gives business owners the power to track every purchase. Checks and MoneyCodes Here are some examples of how you can use checks to help your drivers when they have unexpected expenses out on the road: Checks and MoneyCodes: WEX offers checks and MoneyCodes which provide immediate payment to the user. This is a great alternative when using the WEX or Fleet One EDGE card isn’t an option. Similar to a personal or company check, these checks are accepted pretty much universally. Here’s how they help you get cash to your truck drivers. You can: Advance funds to drivers immediately Instantly pay lumpers, repair shops, or roadside services Access check cashing information in real time Issue money instantly via the web, a mobile app, or a phone Integrate transactions with your back-office or interface directly with dispatch software Learn more about getting cash to your drivers with checks and money codes! Download now Cashing different types of checks while on the road Since most banks have limited hours of operation, the ability to withdraw funds or cash a check at a truck stop is essential for your drivers. Truck drivers’ schedules require that services be available 24/7. A limitation is that many of these convenient stores and stations on the highway don’t cash money orders, tax refunds, insurance checks, third-party foreign travelers, or gift checks. Walmart and other large supermarket chains, on the other hand, will often cash many of these types of checks. At Walmart, go to the customer service desk in the MoneyCenter for check cashing services.They will also cash money orders up to $5,000, charging fees from $4 – $8, depending on the amount. Of the 5,206 Walmart locations across the US, many offer 24-hour check cashing at the service desk. Fraud protection and driver accountability Transaction monitoring and alerts Whether your drivers are new or experienced, fraud is always a challenge for fleet managers . With a fuel card, if any transaction seems out of the ordinary, fleet managers can be automatically notified. These alerts help keep fraudulent activity to a minimum and save your business from having to pay unexpected costs. Monitoring your drivers’ activities in real time helps you ensure they are using the most thoughtful purchasing behavior. Many fleet fuel cards will allow managers to turn off card access immediately when fraudulent activity is detected. The WEX SmartHub App allows managers to stay up-to-date on all fleet card purchase activity, adding a valuable layer of security. Spending controls and driver ID verification The Fleet One EDGE fuel card helps growing fleets save thousands per year in fuel discounts alone. Additionally, the card offers no fuel transaction fees at over 4,000 in-network sites, and big discounts on tires, maintenance, wireless plans, and more . Easy-to-use spending controls help prevent misuse and fraud. The cards automatically provide you with the valuable data and reporting you need. WEX’s fleet card helps mid-to-large fleets better manage and control fuel purchases. With this card you get real-time fuel card data integration and greater insights into purchasing and volume performance. Consolidating transactions onto a single platform is ideal. It gives fleets one place to manage purchases, driver pay, settlement, and cash advances. Year-end reporting and tax prep for trucking fleets The reporting and tracking features that come with most cards provide administrative savings for your trucking business. As an example, fleet managers can save significant time on bookkeeping, expense planning, and tax preparation with the tools that automatically come with a fuel card. WEX offers many different fuel cards for any size business . In addition to the sophisticated reporting features, managers can access GPS tracking with a mobile app that allows them to see the location of vehicles at any time. Factoring: Keeping cash flow moving WEX Capital keeps your fleet vehicles moving by accelerating your company’s cash flow at the lowest industry rates. If your business is experiencing a cash crunch, you get access to cash within 24 hours. Factoring is not a loan and there are no banks involved. The WEX Capital money you receive is already owed to you from your accounts receivable. With the WEX factoring-funded fuel cards , funds come from your factored invoice and go directly to your fuel card account. Fleet managers and business owners factor as many or as few invoices as they need. Additionally, customer service representatives make recommendations based on needs. Learn more on how to better manage your over-the-road fleet: Fuel card FAQs Fraud protection Safety tips Tax prep All fleet cards are not the same, and different types of fuel cards suit the needs of different kinds and sizes of businesses. View WEX’s fleet card comparison chart to see which fleet fuel card is right for you. Apply for a fleet card today! Share

title: GoldMining Announces Updated PEA Highlighting $1.0 Billion After-Tax NPV and 32% IRR at La Mina Project, Colombia
summary: GoldMining Inc. is a public mineral exploration company advancing gold-copper projects in the Americas through exploration, strategic investments, and partnerships.
body_text: GoldMining Announces Updated PEA Highlighting $1.0 Billion After-Tax NPV and 32% IRR at La Mina Project, Colombia Share: Vancouver, British Columbia – April 28, 2026 – GoldMining Inc. (TSX: GOLD; NYSE American: GLDG) (the "Company" or "GoldMining") is pleased to announce the results of an updated preliminary economic assessment ( " PEA " ) on the La Mina Project (the " Project " ), located in Antioquia, Colombia. All currency amounts herein are in US dollars unless otherwise indicated. PEA Highlights1 Enhanced Project Value: The updated PEA incorporates current bench-marked costs and updated base case pricing of $3,500 /oz gold (Au), $4.70/lb copper (Cu) and $40/oz silver (Ag), resulting in a 265% increase in after-tax net present value at 5% discount rate ("NPV5%") from the prior PEA disclosed by the Company for the Project. Strong Base Case Economics: After-tax NPV5% of $1.0 billion and an after-tax internal rate of return ("IRR") of 32.2% and initial payback of approximately 2.7 years. Leverage to Spot Prices: At current spot prices (approximately, $4,775/oz Au, $5.75/lb Cu, and $77/oz Ag), the after-tax NPV5% increases to approximately $1.8 billion with an IRR of 49.1% and initial payback of 1.9 years. High Capital Efficiency: Initial capital expenditures are estimated at $523 million, representing an attractive 0.5x initial capital to base case NPV5% ratio that highlights the Project’s potential for a compelling return on investment. Strong Production Profile: Average annual production of 152.4 koz Au equivalent ("AuEq") over the first five years of operation, and total life of mine ("LOM") production of 1.5 Moz AuEq (comprising 1.2 Moz Au, 2.6 Moz Ag, and 195 Mlbs Cu) over an 11.2 year projected mine life. Resilient Cost Profile: Estimated total cash cost of $872/oz Au and All-In Sustaining Cost ("AISC") of $1,045/oz Au (calculated on a by-product basis). Conventional Operation: The PEA contemplates a conventional open-pit truck-and-shovel operation and a processing rate of 15,000 tonnes per day ("tpd"). A proven processing flowsheet utilizing standard froth flotation and leach circuits achieves high metallurgical recoveries of 91% Au, 80% Cu, and 64% Ag. Significant Portfolio Potential: On a gold equivalent basis, the estimated mineral resources contained in the La Mina PEA account for approximately 9% of the Company’s global Measured and Indicated Resources and 16% of the Inferred Resources (refer to the Company’s Annual Information Form dated February 27, 2026). Alastair Still, CEO of GoldMining commented , “The updated Project PEA highlights the underlying quality of the La Mina porphyry gold-copper mineral system and represents just a small portion of and emphasizes the depth of the GoldMining portfolio of projects that we continue to advance. By capturing current market consensus metals pricing, the PEA conceptualizes a robust $1.0 billion base case project that is characterized with an efficient capital intensity. We’re not simply adjusting for the higher commodity prices; we have confirmed that La Mina is potentially a resilient development opportunity. With these solid base case economics, which improve substantially at spot prices, the Company is excited by the opportunity to further advance and de-risk the Project on the path towards potential future development.” 1 The gold equivalent equations are: AuEq(oz) = Au (g/t) + [Cu(%) x {Cu Price/Au Price} x 22.0462 x 31.1035] + [Ag (g/t) x {Ag Price/Au Price}]. AISC includes mining costs, processing costs, royalties, G&A costs, transportation costs, sustaining capital and closure costs less by-product credits. La Mina PEA Summary The PEA reviewed and refined mine engineering design work completed during the previous (2023) preliminary economic assessment disclosed by the Company, including updating all operating and capital cost estimates following a comprehensive review of technical inputs, and updating metal price assumptions. No other substantive changes were made during the study. The Project, covering 3,208 hectares, is located in the Department of Antioquia, Republic of Colombia, approximately 51 km southwest of Medellin. The Mineral Resource Estimate ( " MRE " ) for La Mina includes the La Cantera, La Garrucha, and Middle Zone porphyry deposits, which are located within 1,000 meters of each other. No additional drilling has been completed at La Mina in support of this updated PEA, therefore the current MRE with effective date December 20th, 2022, remains current in support of the PEA. The PEA considers a conventional drill, blast, load, and haul open pit operation mining an average of 97,000 tpd over the 11.2 year life of mine. It contemplates that resources will be processed at a nominal rate of 15,000 tpd by conventional grinding and flotation to generate a copper concentrate, with tailings of the copper process reporting to a leach circuit to generate gold-silver doré on site. The combined LOM average metallurgical recovery of 91%, 80% and 64% are realized for gold, copper and silver, respectively. The PEA includes on-site development including mining, haul roads, access roads, process facilities, tailings and waste storage facilities, and related ancillary facilities. Construction is anticipated to take approximately two years with an initial capital expenditure of $523.3 million with operations continuing for 11.2 years. Sustaining capital expenditures over the LOM are expected to be approximately $166 million, consisting of a mix of mining capital equipment and staged expansion of the tailings and waste facilities. LOM operating costs are expected to average $29.50/t of material processed. Under the PEA, highest metal production occurs in the initial five years of production averaging 152.4 koz AuEq comprising 126 koz Au, 22.4 Mlbs Cu, and 273 koz Ag annual production. Year 1 production of 176.5 koz AuEq comprises 138 koz Au, 27.0 Mlbs Cu, and 174.8 koz Ag. LOM average production is 137.0 koz AuEq, comprising 107.7 koz Au, 17.0 Mlbs Cu, and 248.6 koz Ag. The LOM average mining rate in the PEA is 5.5 Mt resources per annum and 30.1 Mt waste, which equates to an average LOM strip ratio of 5.5:1. title: PSE&G Prepared for Thunderstorms, Heavy Rain, and Potential Flooding; Ready to Respond to Potential Power Outages
body_text: Newsroom PSE&G Prepared for Thunderstorms, Heavy Rain, and Potential Flooding; Ready to Respond to Potential Power Outages Utility has additional crews and resources in place ahead of today's forecasted severe weather; Follow us on social media for more details (NEWARK, N.J. – July 28, 2026) – PSE&G is closely monitoring forecasts calling for heavy rain and thunderstorms beginning this afternoon continuing into tomorrow morning, bringing the potential for localized flooding and strong wind gusts across much of New Jersey as well as the potential for isolated tornadoes. The company has activated its storm response plan, positioned additional crews and resources throughout its service territory, alerted customers, and is prepared to respond safely and efficiently should severe weather cause power outages. “With strong winds and heavy rains expected to bring flooding to our territory, we have additional line personnel, tree crews and support staff ready to respond in case outages occur,” said Paul Toscarelli, vice president of Electric Operations for PSE&G . “We’ll continue to monitor weather conditions and system performance throughout the event, adjusting our response to best serve customers as conditions evolve.” Throughout the storm, PSE&G will remain in close communication with county and local emergency management officials and other public safety partners to help coordinate response efforts as needed. Our customer-facing teams, including representatives in the call center and across the company’s communications channels, will remain active to provide updates to customers as conditions change. During the early July storms, we delivered over 10 million messages to customers, including pre-storm email messages on how to stay safe and prepare for a storm as well as text alerts and outage updates during the storm. PSE&G encourages customers to prepare before the storm arrives: Charge cell phones and other essential electronic devices. Keep flashlights and fresh batteries readily available. Avoid using candles whenever possible. Secure or bring inside outdoor furniture, umbrellas, grills and other loose objects that could become airborne in strong winds. If you rely on electrically powered medical equipment, have a backup plan in place. Never touch or approach downed power lines . Always assume they are energized and dangerous. Stay at least 30 feet away and report them immediately. Use portable generators only outdoors and well away from windows, doors and vents to prevent carbon monoxide poisoning . Customers who rely on electricity to operate life-sustaining medical equipment should notify PSE&G in advance by visiting pseg.com/life or calling 1-800-436-7734 , and should have a backup plan in the event of an outage. Customers can report outages and monitor restoration progress by: Using the PSE&G mobile app Visiting pseg.com/outagecenter Texting “OUT” to 4PSEG (47734) Calling 1-800-436-PSEG (7734) Customers are encouraged to sign up for outage alerts to receive updates by text, email or phone and follow us on social media: @PSEG on Facebook and Instagram and @PSEGdelivers on X. PSE&G reminds customers that restoration work begins only after conditions are safe for crews to perform their work. During widespread outages, crews first assess damage across the electric system to determine restoration priorities before beginning repairs. Restoration efforts focus first on repairing damage that returns power to the greatest number of customers, while also restoring service to critical facilities such as hospitals, emergency response agencies and other essential infrastructure. PSE&G will continue providing updates through its Outage Center , mobile app and social media channels as conditions warrant. If the severity of the storm or its impacts change significantly, the company will provide additional information as it becomes available. For additional storm safety information, outage updates and restoration information, visit pseg.com/outagecenter . ### About PSE&G Public Service Electric & Gas Co. is New Jersey’s oldest and largest gas and electric delivery public utility, as well as one of the nation’s largest utilities. PSE&G has won the ReliabilityOne® Award for superior electric system reliability in the Mid-Atlantic region for 24 consecutive years. In 2025, for the fourth consecutive year, J.D. Power named PSE&G number one in customer satisfaction for residential electric service in the East among large utilities. PSE&G is a subsidiary of Public Service Enterprise Group Inc., (PSEG) (NYSE:PEG), a predominantly regulated infrastructure company named to the Dow Jones Best in Class Index for North America for 18 consecutive years ( www.pseg.com ). Contacts : DL-ENT-pseg.communications@pseg.com

title: How to Improve Client Retention in Your Law Firm
summary: Most firms lose clients for one simple reason. Learn 4 proven ways to keep them loyal and turn them into your best referral source.
body_text: How to Improve Client Retention in Your Law Firm ‍ Today, law firms are investing in AI and automation to scale more efficiently. But the ones building long-term loyalty? They’re focused on communication. Because at the end of the day, clients don’t just remember what you did, they remember how you made them feel. This is part 1 in our client retention series. This guide will help you build a retention strategy for your firm that blends automation with meaningful human touch. ‍ Step 1: Understand Why Communication Matters Retention isn’t about results alone. How you guide and inform clients along the way plays a key role in client retention and referrals. And the numbers don’t lie: 22.8% of clients leave due to a lack of communication , making it the second most common reason clients fire their law firm (LexisNexis) 82% of legal consumers say timeliness in communication is essential when choosing a lawyer (CallRail) The #1 bar complaint is lack of communication (NationalLawReview) These aren’t small misses. When communication breaks down, clients lose confidence. No matter the outcome of the case, if a client feels left in the dark, they’ll walk away feeling uncared for. And with that, retention and referrals disappear too. ‍ Step 2: Use AI to Support, Not Replace, Your Team The client experience starts long before a case is opened, it begins at intake. And too often, that first impression gets lost to missed calls, long wait times, or clunky forms. This is where AI can make a real difference for your firm. Tools like Voice AI can greet every caller immediately, capture key information, and route urgent matters to the right person on your team. That means no voicemail black holes, no frustrating delays, just a fast, helpful response from the start. It’s a small shift, but it can dramatically improve how potential clients feel about your firm from the first interaction. But here’s the key: AI is a support tool, not a replacement. The human touch and empathy remains essential for client trust. If you want to improve your intake process using AI and increase Google Reviews, check out part 1 from Matador Solutions (experts in legal digital marketing). ‍ Step 3: Automate to Inform Clients shouldn’t have to guess what’s going on. That’s where automation and tools like Hona’s client portal can help. When customized well, client portals become communication hubs that help clients feel informed and cared for: Automate case updates, event reminders, and messages For your firm- these keep clients in the loop without adding to your team’s workload. For your clients- frequent updates and messages reduce anxiety, limit follow-up questions, and show your clients you’re on top of their case. Use automation to deliver more personal touches Like birthday messages or check-ins during slow periods. (Below is an example of a real Google review from a firm that uses the automated birthday messages in Hona). Google review of a firm that uses a client portal for automation ‍ Small, thoughtful gestures go a long way in a profession where communication often feels transactional.The goal is to make automation feel warm and human, not robotic. This builds client trust and keeps them engaged. ‍ Step 4: Empower Your Team to Deliver Exceptional Client Care There are moments in every client relationship where tone and empathy matter more than speed. Delays. Sensitive updates. Gray areas. These are not moments to let automation take over. Even a short call or personal note can reinforce trust and show clients that someone’s paying attention. With the every day communications taken care of, your team can spend more time providing personalized support. But tech alone won’t cut it. Your team still needs the tools, training, and clarity to communicate with consistency and care. When you combine smart systems with a team that knows how to show up, that’s when you start building real client loyalty. ‍ Conclusion: Build a Simple System That Works You don’t need a major overhaul to improve retention.
